full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the impugned order refusing to restore the civil revision No. 1827 of 1991 discharged for default. 

 2. Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Additional Attorney-General appearing for the petitioners, submits that in view of the filing of two revisions against the impugned order of the Court of appeal below in respect of the selfsame suit for declaration of title in the suit land, the other civil revision No. 1826 of 1991 still remaining pending, the discharge of the instant Rule for failure to deposit the requisites would adversely affect the decision in the suit in case of the other Rule being made absolute resulting thereby a conflicting decision operating differently between the parties in respect of the suit land subject-matter of a single suit for declaration of title. The learned Additional Attorney-General has further submitted that the latches in taking steps was not due to the negligence of the law officer concern but was due to the delay in obtaining sanction for deposit of the requisite and, as such, the Rule is required to be restored for ends of justice. 

 3. It appears that two Rules were issued against the judgment and decree of the appellate Court dated 28-7-1990 arising out of decree dated 31-8-1985 in a suit for declaration of title against the petitioners and both the Rules were ordered to be heard together and accordingly rules were issued upon plaintiffs. The matter came up before the Lawzima Court on 6-1-1992 but no one appeared on that date whereupon the Registrar passed an order for issuance of fresh notice by registered post directing to put in requisites with correct postal address within 20-1-1991 and failure to deposit the same by the date fixed the matter came up before the Court on 20-1-1992. As none appeared the Court accordingly passed the order allowing three weeks’ time to put in the requisite failing which the Rule shall stand discharged. Accordingly the Rule stood discharged after expiry of three weeks with effect from 20-7-1992 as no steps were taken. Thereafter, the petitioner did not take any steps within reasonable time but after a lapse of about 7 years on the plea that the matter was misplaced, an application for restoration vacating the order dated 20-7-1992 was filed. The High Court Division did not find the explanation satisfactory. The suit of the plaintiffs was decreed on 31-8-1985 and the appeal there from was dismissed on 27-8-1990. The Rule was discharged in 1992 but there was not explanation for unusual delay thereby accruing a vested right in the respondent. The High Court Division did not find favour with the explanation of long unusual delay in order to deprive a vested right to the plaintiff. The High Court Division in exercise of its discretion rejected the prayer for restoration of the Rule discharged for default.
